questions.question: What is the minimum number of offers before committing? If a single offer is sometimes acceptable, under which conditions (amount below a threshold, sole-source component, urgency), and who must justify or approve it?
questions.why: The brief states both 'at least three offers' and 'a single offer is acceptable for any purchase'. Rule R3 cannot be enforced until this is settled.

questions.question: What is the approval limit? Is it one amount for all buyers or set per buyer, and in which currency? Is the comparison made on the order amount before or after tax?
questions.why: Rule R2 and the place_purchase_order precondition depend on the threshold.

questions.question: Who maintains the blocked list, and in which system? Should an order already in progress be stopped if its supplier becomes blocked?
questions.why: Rule R1 depends on a reliable, current blocked flag.

questions.question: Can one requirement be split across several purchase orders or suppliers?
questions.why: This determines the cardinality between Requirement and PurchaseOrder and how the approval limit applies (per order or per requirement).

questions.question: Can the head of purchasing approve their own orders, and who approves if the head of purchasing is the buyer or is absent?
questions.why: The brief does not say how to avoid self-approval or how to escalate.

roles.name: buyer
roles.description: Collects and compares offers, negotiates, and places purchase orders up to their approval limit.

roles.name: head_of_purchasing
roles.description: Approves or rejects purchase orders above a buyer's approval limit.

agents.name: sourcing_assistant
agents.description: Helps buyers record offers, prepare comparisons and draft purchase orders. Checks the blocked list and the approval limit, and routes orders above the limit for human approval. It does not approve orders.

integrations.description: Routes orders above the limit to the head of purchasing.
Issues the purchase order to the supplier and checks the blocked list.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: The blocked list is represented as a boolean flag on Supplier.
The approval limit can be stored on, or derived for, each purchase order from the buyer who places it.
A purchase order is based on exactly one accepted offer.

unknowns: The value of the approval limit and whether it varies by buyer
The true minimum-offer rule and its exceptions
The source system for the blocked list, suppliers and purchase orders
Whether approval decisions need a recorded justification or a deadline
How negotiation outcomes (revised offers) should be recorded

understanding.summary: The purchasing department sources components. For each requirement, buyers gather supplier offers, compare price, lead time and contractual conditions, negotiate, and commit with a purchase order. Orders above a buyer's approval limit need approval from the head of purchasing. Blocked suppliers must never receive an order, and there is an offer-count rule whose minimum is contradictory.
understanding.outcome: Components are sourced through compliant, well-compared purchase orders committed within approval authority.
out_of_scope: How suppliers are added to or removed from the blocked list
Supplier qualification and contract management beyond the offer's conditions
